findings.target: docs/c-api/OWNERSHIP.md defines all six (Transferred: 'CNA consumes caller ownership on successful return; failure leaves caller ownership unchanged'). Three routes consume a handle: modules/c-api/include/CNA/C/engine_layer.h::cna_post_process_effect_pass_create_owning ('On success the effect handle is consumed ... On failure the caller keeps the effect'), cna_post_process_chain_add_owned_pass and cna_skybox_set_owned_environment ('On success it is released from the runtime and must not be used again'); modules/c-api/src/CnaCApiEngineLayer.cpp releases the handle after every check that can fail in all three (CreateEffectPass, cna_post_process_chain_add_owned_pass, cna_skybox_set_owned_environment). Their @param lines for pass/environment say 'invalid on return whether or not the call succeeded', which the code and the same headers' description contradict. Other 'ownership' wording that is not a consume: cna_media_queue_add appends a copy; cna_effect_material_retain_parameter_texture_ext retains (header title says 'takes ownership' but the caller may still release its own handle); cna_skinned_model_ext_create_move / _move_assign leave the source valid but empty.
findings.site_now: development/handbook/update-the-c-api.html names the six categories but gives no rule for any of them, and deep-dives/reference/native-c-api.html (the contract page) covers buffers, callback contexts, retention, devices and routes but never mentions a route that invalidates a handle the caller holds (site-wide search for add_owned_pass, create_owning, set_owned_environment and 'takes ownership' in the C API pages finds nothing). A binding that treats every handle as owned until its own destroy route will double-release these three. The @param/description contradiction is not in Known Issues (candidate documentation bug).

fix.html:
Routes that consume a handle

OWNERSHIP.md gives every handle and pointer parameter one of six categories: owned (release exactly once before runtime shutdown), borrowed (usable only for the call or callback), retained (CNA keeps an extra reference or a copy), transferred (CNA consumes ownership on a successful return), callback context (the caller keeps the void* valid until unregistration completes) and caller buffer (caller storage for the whole call; CNA stores it only where the route says it copies or retains). Transfer is the rare one, and it is the only category that makes a handle you still hold stop existing.

At 009d40f5 three routes, all in the CNAEXT engine layer, take an object over from a handle: cna_post_process_effect_pass_create_owning (the pass owns the effect), cna_post_process_chain_add_owned_pass (the chain owns the pass) and cna_skybox_set_owned_environment (the skybox owns the cube map). Each releases the caller's handle from the registry on success, so the caller must not destroy it afterwards, and each is a separately named route rather than a flag on the borrowing form (cna_post_process_chain_add_pass, cna_skybox_set_environment). The implementations release the handle only after every check that can fail, so a refusal (an invalid handle, an effect from another game, a pass that is still lending its effect) leaves it valid and still yours: read the result before dropping it. The @param lines of cna_post_process_chain_add_owned_pass and cna_skybox_set_owned_environment say the handle is 'invalid on return whether or not the call succeeded'; the code does not do that and the rest of the same comments contradict it (by reading; no test exercises a refused hand-over). Routes that only copy or retain never consume: cna_media_queue_add appends a copy of the song, and cna_effect_material_retain_parameter_texture_ext lets a material keep a texture alive while the caller may still release its own handle. The move routes (cna_skinned_model_ext_create_move, cna_skinned_model_ext_move_assign) leave their source valid but empty. A binding should model 'moved-from on success' for the first three instead of treating every handle as owned until its own destroy call.
